questions.q: In what book were the descendants of Levi and their leaders of families recorded?
questions.a: They were recorded in the Book of the Events of Days until the days of Johanan.

questions.q: Why did the people seek out the Levites at the dedication of the wall of Jerusalem?
questions.a: The people brought the Levites to Jerusalem to perform the dedication ceremony.

questions.q: What did the priests and Levites do for the celebration?
questions.a: The priests and Levites purified themselves, and then purified the people, the gates, and the wall.

questions.q: Where did the leaders of Judah go on the day of celebration?
questions.a: The leaders went up to the top of the wall.

questions.q: What were the two large choirs that Nehemiah appointed supposed to do?
questions.a: The two large choirs were supposed to give thanks.

questions.q: Where did the first choir go?
questions.a: One choir went to the right on the wall toward the Dung Gate.
The singers sang with Jezrahiah as overseer.

questions.q: Why did they offer great sacrifices that day, and rejoice?
questions.a: They offered great sacrifices that day, and rejoiced, because God had made them rejoice with great rejoicing.

questions.q: Who was assigned to work the fields near the towns?
questions.a: The men who were appointed to be in charge of the storerooms were assigned to work the fields near the towns.

questions.q: When did all Israel give the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers?
questions.a: In the days of Zerubbabel and in the days of Nehemiah, all Israel gave the daily portions for the singers and the gatekeepers.

commentary.text: The priests and Levites that returned.
The officers of the temple settled.

Verses 1–26 It is a debt we owe to faithful ministers, to remember our guides, who have spoken to us the word of God. It is good to know what our godly predecessors were, that we may learn what we should be.

All our cities, all our houses, must have holiness to the Lord written upon them. The believer should undertake nothing which he does not dedicate to the Lord. We are concerned to cleanse our hands, and purify our hearts, when any work for God is to pass through them. Those that would be employed to sanctify others, must sanctify themselves, and set themselves apart for God. To those who are sanctified, all their creature-comforts and enjoyments are made holy. The people greatly rejoiced. All that share in public mercies, ought to join in public thanksgivings.

When the solemnities of a thanksgiving day leave such impressions on ministers and people, that both are more careful and cheerful in doing their duty, they are indeed acceptable to the Lord, and turn to good account. And whatever we do, must be purified by the blood of sprinkling, and by the grace of the Holy Spirit, or it cannot be acceptable to God.
